target_frame.title: Repeat purchase decline for a refill service
target_frame.problem: A small household-cleaning refill service has acquired more first-time customers but fewer of them place a second order within eight weeks. The product team must choose what to investigate and which limited change to try before its next purchasing commitment.
known_context: Customers choose home delivery or a neighborhood collection point and can buy a starter container or refill an existing one.
Order records contain product, quantity, fulfillment option, discount and date. They do not establish how quickly a household uses the product.
First-order promotions and two new collection points were introduced during the same quarter.
Customer-support messages mention leaks, collection hours and confusion about refilling, but most customers send no message.
The team can invite a limited set of customers to voluntary follow-up and can change one fulfillment or communication process for a month.
target_frame.uncertainty: A missing second order may indicate dissatisfaction, unused stock, a different expected purchase interval, inconvenience or another cause. The team does not know which explanations account for the change.
target_frame.decision_need: Develop a discriminating inquiry and a bounded product or service decision without treating nonpurchase or complaint frequency as a direct measure of satisfaction.
constraints: No mandatory subscription or unsolicited repeated contact.
The purchasing decision is due in five weeks; major packaging redesign is unavailable in that period.

source_instrument.state: Multiple sequential records were formed over overlapping periods under partly shared external influences, but one or more records have uncertain calendar placement or may contain missing or anomalous increments.
source_instrument.operation: Compare the ordered pattern of increments across independently dated or overlapping records and shift their relative alignment until distinctive multi-year patterns correspond consistently across specimens.
source_instrument.signal: A particular alignment produces repeated matching temporal patterns across records and exposes otherwise inconsistent missing, extra, or misassigned increments.
source_instrument.inference: The matching alignment supports assigning specific temporal positions to previously uncertain increments and extending or checking the chronology across overlapping records.
source_instrument.limit: Local growth disturbances, weak shared environmental signal, short or repetitive patterns, measurement error, incorrect reference chronologies, and insufficient overlap can produce ambiguous or false alignments.

S001.text: Multiple sequential records were formed over overlapping periods under partly shared external influences, but one or more records have uncertain calendar placement or may contain missing or anomalous increments.

S002.text: Compare the ordered pattern of increments across independently dated or overlapping records and shift their relative alignment until distinctive multi-year patterns correspond consistently across specimens.

S003.text: A particular alignment produces repeated matching temporal patterns across records and exposes otherwise inconsistent missing, extra, or misassigned increments.

S004.text: The matching alignment supports assigning specific temporal positions to previously uncertain increments and extending or checking the chronology across overlapping records.

S005.text: Local growth disturbances, weak shared environmental signal, short or repetitive patterns, measurement error, incorrect reference chronologies, and insufficient overlap can produce ambiguous or false alignments.

P001.text: Act on overlapping customer histories: dated order sequences and, for a limited consenting sample, reconstructed sequences of receipt or collection, product use, stock remaining, attempted refilling and subsequent purchase.

P002.text: Order dates provide calendar anchors; recalled events may have uncertain dates, omitted episodes or unusual quantities.

P003.text: Sample both repeat purchasers and nonpurchasers across fulfillment options, starter versus existing containers, discounts and acquisition periods.

P004.text: Shared service conditions might produce recurring temporal patterns, but neither comparable household consumption nor a common response to those conditions is established.

P005.text: During week one, construct a calendar-dated order reference and separate weekly event sequences for participating households.

P006.text: Use one voluntary invitation offering an interview and optional agreed follow-up; do not repeatedly contact nonrespondents.

P007.text: Ask about actual use, remaining stock, alternative purchases and service encounters without presuming dissatisfaction.

P008.text: Preserve unknown intervals and distinguish reported events from recorded orders.

P009.text: Compare overlapping histories, shifting only uncertain recalled segments within their reported date ranges until distinctive ordered patterns correspond across several independently anchored histories.

P010.text: Keep known order dates fixed, preserve event order, and compare alternative alignments rather than selecting the most convenient one.

P011.text: For example, test whether uncertain recollections of a failed collection fall into a consistently dated sequence of low stock, collection difficulty and delayed purchase.

P012.text: Also compare time since first order and since reported depletion, without replacing calendar dates.

P013.text: Where a mismatch suggests a missing episode, seek clarification through an already agreed follow-up; do not insert an event merely to improve the match.

P014.text: Stop alignment when alternatives remain equally plausible, overlap is insufficient or the first week ends.

P015.text: If a recurring, corroborated sequence identifies an actionable fulfillment or communication obstacle, choose one corresponding process change for the remaining month: for example, clearer refill instructions for evidenced confusion, or a feasible collection-hours adjustment for evidenced access difficulty.

P016.text: Prespecify its intended observable effect and, where feasible, randomly allocate eligible customers or collection periods to the changed process and the current process.

P017.text: If no explanation is sufficiently discriminated, stop short of choosing a purported remedy and use the purchasing deadline to make a cautious, explicitly uncertain commitment from confirmed orders and reported stock needs.

P018.text: Look for one permissible alignment that repeatedly matches distinctive sequences across independently anchored households and makes previously inconsistent timing intelligible.

P019.text: Record whether competing alignments also fit.

P020.text: A candidate signal could be low stock followed by an unsuccessful collection attempt and a later order, recurring around the same service conditions; another could be continued stock availability without a refill attempt.

P021.text: These are proposed observations, not findings.

P022.text: Apparent missing or anomalous episodes become questions for corroboration, not established facts.

P023.text: During the trial, observe the specific targeted step—such as successful collection or correct completion of refilling—alongside remaining stock, attempted purchases and dated orders.

P024.text: Record participation and missing follow-up separately from outcomes.

P025.text: A distinctive, independently corroborated alignment can narrow the calendar position of uncertain customer events, check reconstructed histories and connect overlapping observation periods.

P026.text: It can thereby distinguish some households that have not yet needed a refill from households whose need preceded a documented obstacle.

P027.text: Repeated correspondence supports prioritizing a mechanism for a bounded trial; it does not establish that the mechanism explains the overall decline.

P028.text: A credible comparison during the month can support a provisional decision about the changed process within the tested group and conditions.

P029.text: At five weeks, base the purchasing commitment on confirmed demand, observed stock and usage information, trial results and explicit uncertainty.

P030.text: Use any consented later observation to assess second orders once cohorts have actually completed eight weeks.

P031.text: Household size, usage, initial quantity, alternative purchasing and local service events can disrupt shared patterns.

P032.text: Short, repetitive sequences, recall and measurement errors, incorrect anchors, insufficient overlap and searching many shifts can create false matches.

P033.text: Do not claim precise dates when only a range is supported, or extend a chronology beyond supported overlaps.

P034.text: Promotions and new collection points began in the same quarter, so matching timing alone cannot separate their effects.

P035.text: Voluntary participants and support-message senders may differ from other customers; neither complaint frequency, silence nor nonpurchase directly measures satisfaction.

P036.text: A month's trial cannot establish eight-week repeat purchase for newly exposed customers, and small or nonrandom comparisons may remain inconclusive.

P037.text: Stop or revise the trial if it creates observed fulfillment problems or cannot be delivered as specified; document departures before interpreting outcomes.

P038.text: Major packaging redesign is unavailable, and evidence of leaks may warrant further investigation without implying that the permitted process change will resolve them.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Recorded order dates provide calendar anchors for customer histories.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 establishes that order records contain dates, supporting their use as calendar reference points within customer histories. This does not establish the accuracy of every recorded date or date unrecorded events, neither of which the assertion claims.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Recalled customer events may have uncertain dates.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S001 concerns uncertain temporal placement in the source records; it supplies no premise about customer recollections. P002 repeats the mapping assertion without independently supporting it. Although plausible and cautiously phrased, the claim lacks cited support at the stated customer-sample scope; transferring uncertainty from the source records requires an unstated inference.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Recalled customer histories may omit episodes.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S001 concerns potentially missing increments in the source records; it does not establish omissions in recalled customer histories. P002 repeats the mapped assertion without independent support. Although 'may' asserts only a possibility, transferring the source-record limitation to customer recall requires an unstated substantive premise. The cited material therefore does not warrant the assertion at its stated scope.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Recalled customer histories may contain unusual quantities.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: P002 repeats the assertion without supplying independent support. T001 establishes that orders record quantities, but provides neither a baseline for unusual quantities nor evidence concerning quantities in reconstructed histories. The qualified wording “may” does not supply the missing warrant; this does not establish that the assertion is false.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Shared service conditions might produce recurring temporal patterns across customer histories.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S001 describes shared influences in the source setting but supplies no premise connecting service conditions to recurring customer-history patterns. P004 repeats the possibility without independently supporting it. Although cautiously phrased, the assertion requires an unsupported substantive transfer; this does not establish that the possibility is false.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Comparable consumption across households is not established.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 explicitly states that order records do not establish how quickly households use the product and leaves unused stock and differing purchase intervals unresolved. This warrants withholding an assumption of comparable consumption in cross-household temporal comparisons; it does not establish that consumption differs or is incomparable.

obligation_verdicts.subject: A common household response to shared service conditions is not established.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The target provides order records and limited support messages, but leaves household usage and explanations for nonpurchase unresolved. These do not establish a common temporal response to shared service conditions across households. The limitation appropriately identifies missing support without claiming that household responses necessarily differ.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Unknown intervals must remain represented as unknown in reconstructed histories.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule has a determinate trigger—an interval is unknown during construction or comparison of household histories—and a determinate response: preserve its representation as unknown. This prospective constraint is internally coherent and requires no particular notation to specify the required behavior. P008 supplies the rule being assessed, without establishing observed compliance.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Reported customer events must be distinguished from recorded orders.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule applies when incorporating customer reports and recorded orders into reconstructed histories and prescribes preserving their distinct evidential provenance. Its trigger and required response are sufficiently determinate and internally coherent. A general reliability ranking or particular labeling format is unnecessary at this scope. P008 supplies the prospective instruction, without establishing that it has been followed.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Alignment may shift only uncertain recalled segments, and only within their reported date ranges.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively constrains proposed alignment adjustments: only uncertain recalled segments are eligible, and shifts must remain within their reported date ranges. These eligibility and boundary conditions provide a determinate, internally coherent permission rule. Without a reported range, the rule supplies no permission to shift; further handling need not be specified at this scope. This judgment concerns the rule's structure, not whether alignment is informative or has succeeded.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Shift the relative calendar placement of uncertain recalled customer segments during history comparison.
unresolved_conditions: Customer histories must contain sufficiently distinctive, overlapping patterns tied to shared calendar conditions, rather than merely similar household purchase or consumption stages.
Independent anchors and corroboration must adequately constrain candidate shifts within reported date ranges and distinguish competing alignments.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposed bounded shifts preserve the source mechanism of comparing ordered patterns through relative temporal alignment while retaining fixed dates and event order. Such alignment could clarify whether refill need preceded a service obstacle, which is relevant to the target inquiry. However, the packet does not establish a shared temporal signal, sufficient overlap or reliable discrimination among alignments in customer histories. The restrictions define a plausible comparison procedure but do not themselves establish its diagnostic applicability or successful results.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Known order dates must remain fixed during alignment.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule has a determinate trigger—aligning household histories containing known order dates—and a determinate response: leave those dates unchanged. It coherently restricts permissible adjustments while allowing uncertain recalled segments to shift within their reported ranges. This assesses the prospective rule's structure, without asserting date reliability, compliance or alignment effectiveness.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Alignment must preserve event order.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively governs each proposed alignment adjustment: preserve the sequence of events and exclude adjustments that reorder them. P010 explicitly states this constraint, giving a determinate trigger and prescribed response at the stated scope. Handling uncertainty about event order itself is unspecified, but this does not undermine the coherent prohibition on changing event order during alignment. This judgment concerns the rule's structure, not observed compliance or the usefulness of alignment.

obligation_verdicts.subject: A candidate alignment should permissibly and repeatedly match distinctive ordered sequences across several independently anchored histories while making previously inconsistent timing intelligible.
unresolved_conditions: Customer histories must contain a sufficiently shared temporal signal, rather than merely similar household purchase cycles occurring at unrelated calendar times.
Histories must have reliable independent anchors and sufficient overlap and distinctiveness to discriminate candidate alignments.
Correspondence must withstand comparison with alternative alignments and independent corroboration, with shifts restricted to supported uncertainty ranges.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposed comparison preserves the source mechanism's ordered-pattern matching, constrained relative alignment and reconciliation of uncertain timing. It could provide relevant information about whether refill need preceded a service obstacle. However, dated orders do not establish consumption timing or a shared cross-household temporal signal. The source explicitly identifies weak shared signals, repetitive patterns and insufficient overlap as causes of false alignment. The proposal specifies suitable safeguards but supplies no observations establishing these applicability conditions. Its license is therefore conditional; neither a successful alignment nor an explanation of the purchase decline is established.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Alternative alignments must be compared and competing fits recorded rather than selecting an alignment for convenience.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Comparing candidate alignments and retaining competing fits faithfully implements the source mechanism's consistency checks and addresses its risk of ambiguous or false alignment. For the target inquiry, this can reveal whether reconstructed customer-event timing remains ambiguous, which is relevant to discriminating explanations for nonpurchase. No formal ranking criterion is supplied, so the procedure alone cannot establish a preferred alignment. This judgment licenses the proposed comparison; it does not establish that comparisons occurred or that informative shared patterns exist.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Low stock followed by unsuccessful collection and a later or delayed order, recurring around the same service conditions, is a proposed sequence against which uncertain collection recollections can be tested.
unresolved_conditions: Overlapping, independently anchored histories must provide sufficiently distinctive shared temporal patterns to discriminate permissible alignments; a common event order alone is insufficient.
Calling a subsequent order delayed requires evidence of household need or an expected purchase interval.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The candidate observation is relevant to distinguishing collection difficulty from lack of refill need. The transferred mechanism, however, depends on distinctive temporal correspondence across anchored or overlapping records. The packet does not establish that this short sequence supplies that correspondence; repetitive patterns or weak shared signals can yield false matches. Order records also do not establish consumption speed, so later purchase alone cannot establish delay. The sequence is therefore conditionally licensed as an alignment test, without establishing its occurrence or explaining the overall decline.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Continued stock availability without a refill attempt is another proposed candidate signal.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposed observation is relevant to investigating unused stock as an explanation for nonpurchase. However, as specified, it does not instantiate the transferred mechanism: matching distinctive ordered patterns across overlapping records to resolve uncertain timing. Continued availability without an attempt supplies no distinctive alignment signal by itself; repetitive patterns can yield ambiguous matches. Its explicit status as a proposal avoids claiming a finding but does not establish the required mechanism fidelity.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Time since first order and time since reported depletion should supplement, without replacing, calendar-date comparisons.
unresolved_conditions: Reported depletion must be sufficiently dated to support elapsed-time comparisons, with uncertainty retained.
Correspondence in elapsed time must remain distinguishable from shared calendar timing and must not independently justify chronology assignments.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The supplementary comparisons are relevant to distinguishing purchase intervals from delays after stock depletion, while retaining calendar comparisons preserves the transferred mechanism's temporal anchors. However, the target records do not establish consumption or depletion timing. Aligning households by first order or depletion can produce similar elapsed-time patterns without the shared calendar correspondence required for chronology inference. The proposal is therefore licensed as an auxiliary comparison under the stated conditions, not as demonstrated alignment success.

obligation_verdicts.subject: An apparent missing or anomalous episode is a question for corroboration rather than an established fact; a mismatch suggesting an omission calls for clarification through an already agreed follow-up.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Alignment can expose inconsistencies, but ambiguous or false alignments can also arise from disturbances, measurement error or insufficient overlap. A mismatch therefore warrants corroboration without establishing an omitted episode. The target permits voluntary follow-up and prohibits unsolicited repeated contact, supporting clarification through already agreed contact. This limitation asserts neither an actual omission nor successful corroboration.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Seek clarification of a mismatch suggesting a missing episode through an already agreed follow-up.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Within the stated scope, clarification faithfully implements the mechanism's checking of potentially missing increments while respecting its vulnerability to false alignments. Voluntary follow-up can seek information about use, stock or service encounters that order records alone cannot establish, making it relevant to distinguishing explanations for nonpurchase. The mismatch licenses inquiry, not insertion of an episode or a conclusion that an omission occurred. No successful clarification or recovered event is asserted.

obligation_verdicts.subject: An event must not be inserted merely to improve an alignment.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively governs revisions: when an event's insertion is justified solely by improving alignment, the prescribed response is to refrain from inserting it. The trigger and prohibition are sufficiently determinate and internally coherent. P013 supplies the rule's wording, without establishing observed compliance or effectiveness.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Alignment should stop if alternative alignments remain equally plausible.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively links a recognizable epistemic trigger—alternative alignments remaining tied after comparison—to a definite response: stop alignment. Comparing alternatives and recording competing fits makes this structure coherent within the first-week inquiry. Although no formal plausibility score is specified, the qualitative tie condition is sufficiently determinate at this scope. This judgment does not establish that a tie has occurred or that alignment is informative.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Alignment should stop if overlap is insufficient.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule is prospective and prescribes a clear response: stop alignment. However, the packet provides neither a minimum overlap nor a qualitative assessment procedure for deciding when overlap is insufficient. The cited limitations do not define that trigger. Thus, the rule is internally coherent but lacks the sufficiently determinate trigger required by this contract.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Alignment must stop when the first week ends.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule specifies a determinate prospective trigger—the end of the inquiry's first week—and a determinate response—stop alignment. P014 makes this deadline an independent stopping condition, so earlier stopping conditions do not conflict with it. This establishes a coherent operational time bound without implying that alignment succeeds or an explanation is discriminated.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If a recurring, corroborated sequence identifies an actionable fulfillment or communication obstacle, choose one corresponding process change for the remaining month.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposition is a prospective decision rule: its trigger requires recurrence, corroboration and identification of an actionable obstacle; its response requires selecting one corresponding process change for a bounded month. These qualitative criteria leave judgment but sufficiently specify the decision structure at the stated scope. This judgment does not establish that the trigger has occurred or that the selected change would be effective.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Try one fulfillment or communication process change corresponding to the identified obstacle.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposed change is relevant to the target and fits its month-long intervention allowance. However, the transferred mechanism aligns sequential records to resolve uncertain chronology; it does not test or alter fulfillment or communication processes. Even if corroboration and actionability conditions are met, this substantive intervention remains an additional operation rather than an instantiation of that mechanism. P015 specifies the proposal but does not establish the missing operational warrant.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Where the recurring, corroborated evidence identifies confusion as an actionable obstacle, clearer refill instructions are a proposed corresponding process change.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: At the stated illustrative scope, the rule specifies a recognizable trigger—recurring, corroborated evidence identifying actionable confusion—and a concrete proposed response: clearer refill instructions. P015 places this response within selection of one process change for the remaining month. This prospective structure is internally coherent without requiring exact instruction wording or establishing that the trigger has occurred or the intervention will work.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Introduce clearer refill instructions as a communication-process trial.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Clearer instructions are relevant to the target's permitted communication changes, but do not instantiate the transferred mechanism: aligning overlapping sequences to resolve uncertain temporal positions. Even if actionable refill confusion is corroborated, changing instructions is a substantive intervention requiring a separate warrant. P015 proposes that intervention; it does not establish its license from the chronology mechanism or demonstrate its effects.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Where the recurring, corroborated evidence identifies access difficulty as an actionable obstacle, a feasible collection-hours adjustment is a proposed corresponding process change.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: At the stated illustrative scope, the rule specifies a prospective trigger—recurring, corroborated evidence identifying actionable access difficulty—and a response: proposing a feasible collection-hours adjustment within P015's selection of one process change for the remaining month. Exact hours and quantitative evidence thresholds are not necessary to make this illustrative decision structure coherent. This judgment does not establish that the trigger has occurred or that the adjustment would be effective.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Adjust collection hours as a fulfillment-process trial.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Adjusting collection hours could address the target problem, but it does not instantiate the transferred mechanism: aligning uncertain sequential records to establish temporal positions. It is a separate substantive intervention. Corroborated access difficulty and feasibility could justify that trial independently, but would not establish mechanism fidelity. The proposed selection condition establishes neither corroboration nor effectiveness.

obligation_verdicts.subject: The selected process change should have its intended observable effect specified in advance.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule has a determinate trigger—selection of a process change for the trial—and a clear prospective response: specify its intended observable effect before the trial. This is internally coherent at the stated scope. An effect size or success threshold is not necessary to make this specification requirement determinate. The judgment does not establish compliance or effectiveness.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Where feasible, eligible customers or collection periods should be randomly allocated between the changed process and the current process.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Random allocation could inform the bounded process decision, but it does not instantiate the transferred mechanism: aligning overlapping records through distinctive temporal patterns to resolve uncertain chronology. It introduces a separate substantive experimental comparison. The feasibility qualifier does not establish that mechanistic connection, and the proposal supplies no observed implementation or results.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If no explanation is sufficiently discriminated, the team should refrain from choosing a purported remedy.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: P017 states a coherent prospective rule: an inconclusive inquiry triggers abstention from choosing a purported remedy. At the stated scope, this qualitative trigger and prescribed response are sufficiently determinate, although no detailed discrimination threshold is supplied. This judgment concerns the rule's structure, not whether its trigger has occurred or the inquiry is informative.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If no explanation is sufficiently discriminated, the purchasing deadline should still be met with a cautious, explicitly uncertain commitment based on confirmed orders and reported stock needs.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposition specifies a prospective fallback: when explanatory uncertainty remains unresolved, make the purchasing commitment by the deadline using named inputs and explicitly acknowledge uncertainty. The trigger and response are sufficiently determinate for this governance scope. Discretion over evidential sufficiency and purchase quantity does not undermine the coherent instruction to proceed under uncertainty. This judgment assesses the rule's structure, not the adequacy of its inputs or its effectiveness.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Trial observation should include the specifically targeted step, such as successful collection or correct refilling, alongside remaining stock, attempted purchases and dated orders.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: These observations are relevant to distinguishing stock availability from service obstacles. However, collecting trial outcomes does not instantiate the transferred mechanism: comparing and shifting overlapping sequences to resolve uncertain temporal placement through distinctive matching patterns. The source licenses chronology reconstruction, not this substantive trial-evaluation operation. Target relevance alone does not satisfy the frozen contract.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Participation must be recorded separately from outcomes.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The proposition is a prospective rule applying whenever participation is recorded in inquiry or trial records. Its prescribed response—record participation separately from outcomes—is sufficiently determinate and internally coherent. Unspecified participation measures do not undermine that separation requirement. P024 supplies the rule's wording, without establishing that it has been followed.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Missing follow-up must be recorded separately from outcomes.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively prescribes a determinate response when follow-up is missing: record that missingness separately from outcomes in inquiry and trial records. This decision structure is internally coherent. A method for analyzing missing outcomes is unnecessary for this narrower recording requirement. P024 supplies the rule's wording, without establishing that it has been implemented.

obligation_verdicts.subject: A distinctive, independently corroborated alignment can narrow the calendar position of uncertain customer events.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The claimed consequence is a limited temporal inference from an explicitly qualifying hypothetical alignment. The source mechanism supports temporal placement through distinctive correspondence with anchored, overlapping records. The proposed restrictions preserve known dates and constrain uncertain segments to reported ranges, making narrowing a defensible consequence rather than a claim of exact dating. Independent corroboration must concern calendar correspondence; similar household event sequences alone would not suffice. The packet establishes neither an actual qualifying alignment nor any achieved narrowing, and the claim does not require either to have occurred.

obligation_verdicts.subject: A distinctive, independently corroborated alignment can check reconstructed customer histories.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The source mechanism licenses checking temporal consistency through distinctive correspondence across anchored, overlapping records. Under the stated hypothetical conditions, this supports checking participating customer histories for timing inconsistencies and possible anomalies. It does not verify every event or establish an omission without corroboration. The proposal asserts neither that a qualifying alignment has occurred nor that any history has already been validated.

obligation_verdicts.subject: A distinctive, independently corroborated alignment can connect overlapping observation periods.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S002 and S004 support temporal linkage through distinctive correspondence across independently dated or overlapping records. The stated independent corroboration and restriction to supported overlaps license this narrow consequence without asserting that a qualifying customer alignment has occurred. S005 limits confidence where overlap or correspondence is inadequate; the claim does not license linkage beyond supported periods.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Such an alignment can distinguish some households that have not yet needed a refill from households whose need preceded a documented obstacle.
unresolved_conditions: Household-specific corroboration must establish refill need or its absence from usage and stock information independently of temporal matching.
Supported event timing must distinguish need preceding the documented obstacle from alternative orderings.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The source mechanism supports temporal placement, which can contribute to the claimed distinction once household need is independently established. It does not itself establish need, and the target explicitly states that order records do not establish consumption speed. Ambiguous alignments may leave the ordering unresolved. The relation is therefore licensed under these conditions, without implying that any household has actually been classified or that an obstacle caused nonpurchase.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Sufficiently informative stock, use and service-event evidence can distinguish absence of refill need from need accompanied by a documented obstacle.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Under the stated sufficiency condition, household-specific stock and use evidence can establish whether refill need arose, while documented service events can establish an accompanying obstacle. Alignment can help resolve timing; it cannot independently establish need or causation. This licenses the limited distinction for some participating households without asserting that qualifying evidence has been collected, that an obstacle caused nonpurchase, or that the distinction explains the population decline.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Repeated correspondence supports prioritizing a mechanism for a bounded trial.
unresolved_conditions: The correspondence must discriminate an actionable mechanism using corroborated evidence of household need and relevant service encounters, rather than temporal matching alone.
Alternative alignments and explanations must be assessed sufficiently to justify the proposed priority.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The source licenses checking chronology and assigning temporal positions, not selecting causal mechanisms. Even hypothetical repeated correspondence therefore needs an additional evidential bridge to mechanism prioritization. The proposed corroborated-obstacle condition could supply that bridge for exploratory trial selection, but its adequacy is unspecified. Target evidence leaves consumption and competing explanations unresolved. This permits conditional prioritization of a hypothesis, without establishing its occurrence, causal truth, or contribution to the overall decline.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Repeated correspondence does not establish that the prioritized mechanism explains the overall repeat-purchase decline.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The alignment mechanism supports temporal placement and chronology checking, not population-level causal attribution. The target includes concurrent promotions and collection-point changes, unknown consumption rates, multiple possible explanations for nonpurchase, and limited voluntary follow-up. Repeated temporal correspondence alone therefore cannot establish a mechanism's contribution to the overall decline. This limitation does not require assuming that any correspondence has actually been observed.

obligation_verdicts.subject: A credible comparison during the month can support a provisional decision about the changed process within the tested group and conditions.
unresolved_conditions: The comparison must measure a decision-relevant process outcome observable within the month and adequately address confounding, missing outcomes and uncertainty.
The decision must rely on that comparison, rather than temporal alignment alone, without implying an established eight-week repeat-purchase effect.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The transferred alignment mechanism supports chronology checking, not intervention-effect inference. A separate credible comparison could support the narrowly scoped provisional decision, but credibility is not operationally specified. The proposed trial procedures suggest a possible bridge without establishing its adequacy or any outcome.

obligation_verdicts.subject: At five weeks, the purchasing commitment should draw on confirmed demand, observed stock and usage information, trial results and explicit uncertainty.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule specifies a determinate trigger—the five-week purchasing deadline—and a prescribed response: ground the commitment in enumerated inputs while making uncertainty explicit. This is a coherent prospective requirement governing the decision's basis. Unspecified input weights and purchase quantity leave discretion without defeating that requirement. The judgment does not establish that those inputs exist or warrant any particular commitment.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Any later observation used to assess second orders should be consented, and assessment should occur once the relevant cohorts have actually completed eight weeks.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively governs later second-order assessment: use consented observations and defer assessment until the relevant cohorts complete eight weeks. These eligibility and timing requirements provide sufficiently determinate triggers and responses and are internally coherent. Uncertain availability of later observations does not undermine the rule's structure or establish that assessment has occurred.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Use consented later observation to assess whether relevant customers placed second orders within eight weeks.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: For consented cohorts with completed outcome windows, this observation is relevant to measuring repeat purchase. However, it does not instantiate the transferred mechanism: comparing distinctive patterns across overlapping records and shifting uncertain temporal alignments to establish chronology. Consent and elapsed observation time support the proposed follow-up but do not supply that mechanism.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Household size, usage, initial quantity, alternative purchasing and local service events can disrupt shared temporal patterns.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The limitation is justified at its stated possibility strength. Household size and usage can affect depletion timing; initial quantities and alternative purchases can alter replenishment intervals; local service events can alter collection and order timing. These mechanisms fit the target's unresolved consumption rates and varied fulfillment conditions, and the source's warning about local disturbances weakening shared patterns. No actual disruption, effect magnitude or explanation of the decline is established.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Short or repetitive sequences can create false matches.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S005 explicitly states that short or repetitive patterns can produce ambiguous or false alignments. The proposition faithfully restates this possible reliability limit without asserting an observed false match or adding a threshold.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Recall and measurement errors can create false matches.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S005 explicitly identifies measurement error as a possible cause of false alignment. Recall errors can similarly distort event timing or sequence, creating apparent correspondence between histories. This mechanism warrants the limited possibility claim; it establishes neither an observed false match nor the frequency or magnitude of errors.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Incorrect calendar anchors can create false matches.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S005 identifies incorrect reference chronologies as a possible cause of false alignments. Incorrect calendar anchors introduce the same failure mechanism: sequences can appear to correspond at wrongly assigned temporal positions. This warrants the stated possibility without establishing that any customer anchor is incorrect or any false match has occurred.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Insufficient overlap can create false matches.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S005 explicitly lists insufficient overlap as a condition that can produce ambiguous or false alignments. The proposition faithfully restates this possibility for candidate alignments without asserting an observed false match or adding a quantitative threshold.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Searching many relative shifts can create false matches.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S002 describes searching relative alignments, and S005 establishes susceptibility to false correspondence. Trying many shifts provides more opportunities for accidental correspondence to appear convincing, justifying the stated possibility of false matches. This does not establish that a false match occurred or specify its probability; no numerical search limit is needed to warrant this qualitative limitation.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Precise event dates must not be claimed when the evidence supports only a range.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Evidence supporting only a date range does not distinguish a precise date within it. S004 ties temporal assignment to supporting alignment, while S005 establishes that alignments can remain ambiguous or false. The limitation appropriately bounds conclusion precision without asserting that any particular customer event has an uncertain date.

obligation_verdicts.subject: A reconstructed chronology must not be extended beyond supported overlaps.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: S004 grounds chronological extension in matching across overlapping records, while S005 identifies insufficient overlap as a source of ambiguous or false alignment. These justify bounding the temporal reach of an alignment-based reconstruction to supported overlaps. No particular overlap or successful reconstruction is established, and the criteria for sufficient support remain unspecified; neither is necessary to warrant this limitation.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Because promotions and new collection points began in the same quarter, matching timing alone cannot separate their effects.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 establishes that both changes were introduced in the same quarter. Temporal correspondence alone supplies no independent comparison that attributes an effect to either change. This justifies the stated limitation without establishing that either change caused the decline or that other evidence could not distinguish their effects.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Voluntary participants may differ from other customers.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 establishes that follow-up is voluntary and limited to invited customers. Willingness to participate can vary with customer experiences or availability, so representativeness is not assured. This justifies the modest possibility stated, without establishing any actual difference, direction, or magnitude.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Customers who send support messages may differ from other customers.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 establishes that support messages describe service problems while most customers send no message. Selection through customers' decisions to contact support justifies possible differences between senders and other customers, without establishing any actual difference, its direction or magnitude.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Complaint frequency does not directly measure satisfaction.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 explicitly requires inquiry without treating complaint frequency as a direct measure of satisfaction. The proposition faithfully restates that limitation within the interpretation of customer-support evidence, without expanding its scope or certainty.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Customer silence does not directly measure satisfaction.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 establishes that most customers send no support message, without establishing their satisfaction or reasons for remaining silent. Absence of contact records communication behavior, not satisfaction, so it cannot distinguish satisfied from dissatisfied silent customers. This justifies the stated direct-measurement limitation without claiming silence has no possible informational value.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Nonpurchase does not directly measure satisfaction.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 explicitly requires avoiding nonpurchase as a direct measure of satisfaction and identifies multiple possible explanations for missing second orders. The proposition faithfully restates this limitation at the stated scope and certainty.

obligation_verdicts.subject: A month's trial cannot establish eight-week repeat purchase for newly exposed customers.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The target specifies an eight-week repeat-purchase outcome and permits a month-long process change. A month provides insufficient follow-up to establish the full eight-week outcome for newly exposed customers. Early repeat purchases can be observed, but customers without a repeat order may still purchase during the remaining weeks.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Small comparisons may remain inconclusive.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The target permits only limited customer follow-up and a bounded trial. Small comparisons can have insufficient precision to distinguish a process effect from sampling variability, justifying the modest claim that they may remain inconclusive. No numerical sample-size threshold or observed inconclusive result is required for this possibility claim.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Nonrandom comparisons may remain inconclusive.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: Nonrandom allocation can leave comparison groups differing in factors that also affect outcomes, making the process change's effect difficult to isolate. The target includes differing fulfillment choices, promotions and unmeasured household usage, providing plausible sources of such confounding. This justifies 'may remain inconclusive' without establishing that any trial has occurred or that every nonrandom comparison is inconclusive.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If the trial creates observed fulfillment problems, it should be stopped or revised.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively links an identifiable trigger—observed fulfillment problems created by the trial—to a bounded response: stop or revise the trial. At this operational scope, allowing either response leaves discretion without making the rule incoherent; continuing unchanged is excluded. No numerical threshold or selection procedure is necessary to express this bound. This judgment does not establish that problems have occurred or that revision would resolve them.

obligation_verdicts.subject: If the trial cannot be delivered as specified, it should be stopped or revised.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule prospectively links an identifiable trigger—inability to deliver the trial according to its specification—to a bounded response: stop or revise it. Leaving discretion between those responses does not undermine its coherence as an operational bound; continuing unchanged is excluded. P037 supplies the rule being assessed, without establishing that any delivery failure has occurred.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Departures from the specified trial must be documented before outcomes are interpreted.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: The rule has a sufficiently determinate trigger—departures from the specified trial—and a clear prescribed response: document those departures before interpreting outcomes. This prospective sequencing requirement is internally coherent at the stated scope. It need not prescribe how documentation changes interpretation to establish this procedural prerequisite, and it does not assert that departures or documentation have occurred.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Evidence of leaks may warrant further investigation.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 identifies support messages mentioning leaks and permits limited voluntary follow-up, supporting leaks as a possible subject of further inquiry. The claim licenses only consideration of investigation; it does not establish confirmed leakage, its contribution to declining repeat purchases, or an effective remedy. The transferred alignment mechanism supports checking chronology, not diagnosing leak causes, and the claim requires no such diagnostic inference.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Evidence of leaks does not imply that the permitted process change will resolve them.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 reports support messages mentioning leaks but establishes neither their cause nor the effectiveness of a fulfillment or communication change in resolving them. The available intervention is limited, and major packaging redesign is unavailable. This justifies withholding an inference of resolution; it does not establish that every permitted process change would be ineffective.

obligation_verdicts.subject: Inquiry into actual use, remaining stock, alternative purchases and service encounters should not presume dissatisfaction.
obligation_verdicts.rationale: T001 supports neutral questioning as relevant to distinguishing possible reasons for nonpurchase. However, the exact proposed operation does not instantiate the transferred mechanism: comparing ordered patterns across anchored, overlapping records and shifting uncertain alignments to resolve temporal placement. P007 specifies an inquiry safeguard, but its inclusion in the mapping does not establish that mechanism fidelity. Target relevance alone does not satisfy this contract.
